messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to create a plot with 3 panels: a BEAST tree, a heatmap, and a dot plot. I applied scale_x_ggtree() to solve the issue with the time axis extending to the heatmap. However, there is a residual undesirable effect that it makes the scale for the other panel (a dot plot, in my case) disappear. This behavior can be seen using the example data from the vignettes as shown with the below code:

# load package
library("ggtree")

#import data
beast_file <- system.file("examples/MCC_FluA_H3.tree", package="ggtree")
beast_tree <- read.beast(beast_file)

genotype_file <- system.file("examples/Genotype.txt", package="ggtree")
genotype <- read.table(genotype_file, sep="\t", stringsAsFactor=F)

# plot tree and heatmap
p <- ggtree(beast_tree, mrsd="2013-01-01") + geom_tiplab(size=2, align=TRUE, linesize=.5) + theme_tree2()
pp <- (p + scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0, 0.3))) %>%
    gheatmap(genotype, offset=8, width=0.6, colnames=FALSE) %>%
        scale_x_ggtree()

# add dot plot data
d1 <- data_frame(id = as_tibble(beast_tree)$label[!is.na <http://is.na>(as_tibble(beast_tree)$label)], val = runif(76, min = 0, max = 10))

p3 <- facet_plot(pp,  panel="dot", data=d1, geom=geom_point, aes(x=val), color='firebrick')

You'll notice in p3, the axes for the tree and heatmap look great, but there is no dotplot axis.

Does anyone have suggestions for how to shorten the x-axis on the dated tree so that it doesn't extend into the heatmap, while keeping a different x-axis on an additional panel?

Best,
Arianna

messages.subject_clean: How to create circular ggtree with multiple gheatmap annotations of continuous variable data?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am in the process of using ggtree to visualize results from 5 different biochemical assays on about 500 microbial isolates.

The tree has been created, and I have the results from all five biochemical assays in a single dataframe.

The biochemical assay data for each isolate are numerical.

What I would like to do is have a single circular tree with a gheatmap that corresponds to results from each biochemical assay of the microbes arranged in outer rings, each with a different color scale.

I found a useful start to a solution here: https://github.com/GuangchuangYu/ggtree/issues/78

I attempted to adapt the code for my specific application, but ran into the issue of the color scale being replaced with each gheatmap implementation, where all gheatmaps are plotted with a single color scale - that being of the final layer. The Github issue linked above uses `scale_fill_manua()` to map discrete annotations in multiple rings, but I cant figure out how to adapt this approach for continuous data variables.

I'd like to know if there is a way to map specific color scales to each of the gheatmaps corresponding to a data from individual assays so that I can have several rings each with a different color scale.

The code I have so far is below:

```{r}

# Make tree
sm_k31_tree <- ggtree(sm_k31_phylo, color = "black", size = 0.3, layout = "fan", open.angle = 6)

# Add gheatmap 1 for biochemical assay 1
pgp1 <- gheatmap(sm_k31_tree, pgp_master[, "BNF", drop=F], width=0.1,
                 colnames_angle = 90, colnames_offset_x =0.4, font.size = 3,
                 color = "black") + scale_fill_gradient(high = "blue", low = "pink")

# Add gheatmap 2 for assay 2
pgp2 <- gheatmap(pgp1, pgp_master[, "ACC", drop=F], offset = 0.5, width = 0.1,
                 colnames_angle = 90, colnames_offset_x = 0.5, font.size = 3,
                 color = "black", high = "green", low = "red")

# create alternate for legend extract
pgp2x <- gheatmap(sm_k31_tree, pgp_master[, "ACC", drop=F], offset = 0.8, width = 0.1,
                 colnames_angle = 90, colnames_offset_x = 0.5, font.size = 2,
                 color = "black", high = "green", low = "red")

# extract legends
require(cowplot)
pgp_leg1 <- get_legend(pgp1)
pgp_leg2 <- get_legend(pgp2x)

# create plot object
pp <- pgp2 + theme(legend.position = "none") + geom_tiplab2(aes(angle=angle), size = 0.8, color = "black", offset = 2)

# plot object with legends
plot_grid(pp, pgp_leg1, pgp_leg2, ncol = 3, rel_widths = c(1, 0.1, 0.1))

```

Is my idea even possible? I imagine there is a way but that my limited knowledge of Rcolor packages is a problem.

Any guidance, advice or help will be greatly appreciated!

Thanks!

Hi,

I have solved your problem.  After running the command g.usnea<-ggtree(Usnea.tree, layout ="fan", aes(color=Phylum), alpha=0.8) %<+% dd
you will see that there is a dataframe layer called g.usnea$data.
If you look at the levels of g.usnea$data$Phylum, you will see 18 factor levels:

> levels(g.usnea$data$Phylum)
 [1] "Acidobacteria"         "Actinobacteria"        "Armatimonadetes"       "Bacteria_unclassified" "Bacteroidetes"         "Chlamydiae"            "Chloroflexi"
 [8] "Cyanobacteria"         "Elusimicrobia"         "Firmicutes"            "Fusobacteria"          "Gemmatimonadetes"      "Planctomycetes"        "Proteobacteria"
[15] "Tenericutes"           "Thermi"                "TM7"                   "Verrucomicrobia"

The 19th factor does not exist as it takes the value <NA> and so does not receive a colour.  You need to create this 19th level.  You do that like this:

levels(g.usnea$data$Phylum) <- c(levels(g.usnea$data$Phylum), 'Ancestral') #This adds a new factor level called 'Ancestral' to the factor levels in g.usnea$data$Phylum

As described in https://yulab-smu.github.io/treedata-book/chapter2.html#ggtree-fortify, you can access the data used in visualization via p$data, which contains node angle in circular layout.

set.seed(2019-02-26)
x = rtree(30)
ggtree(x, layout='circular') + geom_cladelabel(50, 'label X', hjust="right")

messages.subject_clean: Manipulating tree node heights & branch lengths using BEAST node error bars
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am working on a project that requires some automated tree manipulation. I need to write a function that creates two new trees given a BEAST tree with node error bars (95% confidence intervals for divergence time estimates). The two new trees are supposed to have node heights (and corresponding branch lengths) equal to the upper and lower 95CI values of the given tree. So for example, if the given tree has a node at 5±2 Ma, I need to make a tree with the node at 7 Ma and a tree with the node at 3 Ma. All nodes/branches in the tree must be adjusted in this way. The tree is ultrametric so branch lengths must also be adjusted to keep all tips at 0 Ma.

Since this suite of R packages (ggtree, treeio, and tidytree) is the only ones I can find that can utilize BEAST node bar outputs, I'm trying to write the function in here. I'm close, but having some trouble. Here's my code so far:

> # convert the starting tree to a "tibble"
> LCItreetib <- as_tibble(starting_tree)
> r <- nrow(LCItreetib)
> # for every row in the tibble, copy the lower CI value for height, length, and rate

> for (x in 1:r){

>   LCItreetib$rate[x]   <- LCItreetib$rate_0.95_HPD[[x]][2]
> }
> LCItree <- as.treedata(LCItreetib)

Basically I convert the tree into tibble format using tidytree. Then I grab the (in this case) lower estimate of the 95% confidence interval for all node heights, branch lengths, and rates, and replace the starting values with them. This makes a tibble where the actual node heights, branch lengths, and rates now correspond to the lower 95CI estimates of the starting tree. The 95CIs themselves remain unchanged but are not necessary for later analyses.

When I convert the tibble back to a treedata object in the last line is where the trouble begins. I was initially optimistic when I plotted the tree with node height labels like this:
>
> ggtree(LCItree) + geom_text2(aes(subset=!isTip, label=round(height, digits=2)), nudge_y=0.12, nudge_x = -0.65) + theme_tree2()

When I compare the LCI tree to the starting tree, the trees are identical, the only difference being the node height labels themselves. It seems to me that the data that actually changes the tree's displayed shape is stored some other way but I do not know it.
